title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) that measured how often LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals would produce unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action, or unsafe‑execution rate) and whether a preregistered guarded pipeline (validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human‑gate) reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (as actually run: deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a shared single generation—see Disclosure) yielded baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Conservative preregistered sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe (N=300; 28 both‑failed pairs) gives guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. We archive full execution, scoring, and validator artifacts (per‑episode JSON, provider traces, and SHA‑256 hashes). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; therefore the run does not evaluate the preregistered ensemble. All results, failure accounting, and provenance are reported exactly as archived.

sections.introduction: Agentic NetOps workflows convert natural language intent into concrete configuration changes that can be executed automatically. This claim→action pathway turns fluent model text into real system effects and raises a measurable operational risk: plausible but incorrect textual assertions can become harmful actions if executed without trustworthy checks. Prior work recommends generate–validate–repair loops, multimodel consensus, and human gating as mitigations; however, empirical, preregistered measurements with full provenance are rare. We preregistered a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) to quantify whether a guarded pipeline reduces the unsafe‑execution (claim→action) rate versus an unguarded baseline. We emphasize two commitments: (i) preregistration of the experimental design and analysis before observing data; and (ii) archival of every execution artifact (model calls, validator traces, scoring decisions) with SHA‑256 hashes so every reported number is traceable. The executed run and all artifacts are archived (see execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/* files referenced below). The study's core contributions are a preregistered, artifact‑backed paired measurement; transparent disclosure of an execution deviation that prevented evaluation of the preregistered multimodel consensus; and release of per‑episode validator traces and a deterministic execution manifest linking every numeric claim to stored artifacts.
sections.related_work: LLM and agentic systems for NetOps have seen increasing interest: surveys and system papers study intent→configuration translation, tool‑augmented agents, and validator‑assisted architectures. Work on generate–validate–repair and on deterministic validators informs our methodological choices. Taxonomies of agentic failure modes motivate conservative defenses. This study does not claim the first conceptual mitigation; rather, it provides a preregistered, fully archived empirical measurement of a validator‑centric guarded pipeline in a deterministic NetOps simulator, and it documents an execution deviation that prevents ensemble conclusions.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand: We preregistered (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) a paired confirmatory design with N=300 tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial). The primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in safe outcome rates: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Planned analysis: exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes, paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729), and preregistered sensitivity rules that treat failed episodes conservatively as unsafe in sensitivity reporting. Experimental pipeline (preregistered): generate intent→configuration tasks, run baseline (single LLM generation → validator → simulator score), and guarded (preregistered: validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate). All prompts, model calls, raw outputs, validator traces, and logs were to be archived immutably. Execution manifest and file hashes were required for reproducibility (execution/execution_manifest.json contains the full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest). Execution constraints: maximum model calls 600; one automatic retry per failed call; deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 for scoring. Important preregistered inclusion/exclusion: pairs with both modes successfully producing scorable binary outcomes form the primary complete‑pair analysis; pairs with missing outcomes are excluded from the primary analysis but included in sensitivity runs per preregistration.
sections.results: Execution and provenance (artifact values): planned episodes 600; completed episodes 544; failed episodes 56; model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28; stage_counts recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json include {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. Provider‑call audit and per‑file SHA‑256s are archived under execution/execution_manifest.json (see artifact hashes for execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*). Deviation: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was NOT executed in this run; the archived guarded condition corresponds to the deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation per task (execution manifest and provider_call audit show one shared_initial_generation per task and condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}). Primary analysis (complete pairs): N=272 complete pairs (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Observed contingency counts: n11 = 271, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Safe rates on complete pairs: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; this p arises from the contingency pattern (n10=1, n01=0) and indicates no statistical support for a difference under the exact test in the observed data. Missingness and sensitivity: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were therefore excluded from the primary complete‑pair analysis (analysis/missingness_summary.csv; execution/execution_manifest.json records failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28). Preregistered conservative sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe yields N=300: baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Representative artifact examples: per‑episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and task-000001-guarded.json) and raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt) are archived and include the exact JSON fields used to compute reported values; per‑file SHA‑256s are present in execution/execution_manifest.json.
sections.discussion: Primary interpretation (artifact grounded). The executed run shows that a deterministic validator applied to a single LLM generation produced near‑perfect safety on the analyzable pairs (baseline safe ≈99.63%). The observed absolute paired effect is numerically tiny (~0.37 percentage points) and statistically inconclusive (exact McNemar p = 1.0) given the contingency counts and the reduced analyzable sample. Two run‑level operational facts materially limit claims: (1) the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble (validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate) was not executed; the guarded condition in the archived run therefore does not evaluate the preregistered ensemble and H2 from the preregistration is untested by these artifacts (the manifest shows only a single shared_initial_generation per task). We correct all ensemble‑related language and explicitly label any ensemble claim as untested. (2) Provider/model call failures reduced effective N: execution/execution_manifest.json reports failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 and the analysis missingness summary reports 28 failed pairs excluded. The archived provider_calls/* traces and execution/execution_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 recorded in execution_manifest.json) contain the raw failure traces; these traces are the canonical record of failure types. The archived manifest records counts but does not contain a precompiled category breakdown of failure types; therefore we report the concrete, artifact‑backed counts (28 failed hosted model calls; 56 failed episodes; 28 excluded pairs) and point readers to execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*.json for raw failure traces and timestamps (SHA‑256s in execution/execution_manifest.json). Threats to validity: internal — prompt sensitivity, single shared generation per task, and provider call failures that reduced power; construct — the deterministic simulator and validator approximate operational correctness but cannot capture all production risks; external — single declared model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic task bank, isolated simulator. Practical implication: validator‑first architectures can reduce claim→action risk in a controlled simulator, but ensemble and multi‑model claims require a run that actually executes the preregistered ensemble and avoids provider failures; artifacts here document the exact gap and enable replication of the preregistered ensemble under improved call reliability. Reproducibility: every numeric claim is traceable to archived artifacts and SHA‑256s (see execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*; example per‑file SHA‑256 entries are listed under the execution manifest).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and ran a paired measurement of LLM→action safety in a deterministic NetOps simulator and archived full execution and scoring provenance. On the 272 analyzable pairs, the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate on a shared single generation) produced a trivial absolute improvement in safe outcomes (~0.0037) that is inferentially inconclusive. Conservative inclusion of failed pairs produces a similar tiny effect (~0.00333). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation prevented testing the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; that deviation and provider failures materially limit confirmatory claims. We therefore publish exact execution and scoring artifacts (full SHA‑256 manifest recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json) and recommend re‑execution of the preregistered consensus ensemble with improved call reliability and a larger, higher‑fidelity task bank to reach stronger operational conclusions.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).
- Declared hosted model used in execution artifacts: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini").
- Orchestration/adapter used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Deterministic validator used for scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (execution/scoring/*.json include validator_id and validator_version = "deterministic_netops_validator_v5").
- Exact initial master prompt (immutable archived reference): provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. This immutable path+SHA‑256 is the required disclosure reference to the initial master prompt; the archived file provenance/master_prompt.txt is the canonical immutable record and is included in the run archive.
- Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design with N=300 and a guarded defense consisting of a deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human‑gate.
- What actually executed (artifact evidence): execution/execution_manifest.json records planned episodes 600, completed episodes 544, failed episodes 56, model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28, and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. Provider call audit fields show condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}. Per‑episode response and scoring JSONs (execution/responses/*.txt and execution/scoring/*.json) and their SHA‑256 hashes are archived and referenced in the execution manifest. These artifacts demonstrate that the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; the guarded condition in the archived run corresponded to the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a shared single generation. The preregistered consensus hypothesis was therefore not tested by this execution.
- Tools and capabilities permitted and used: deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), hosted LLM provider (declared gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and an isolated deterministic simulator used by the validator. All per‑call provider traces and validator traces were archived under execution/provider_calls/* and execution/scoring/*.json and are included in the full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Preregistration freeze and autonomy boundary: The preregistration was locked before observation (SHA‑256 above). After the autonomy lock the system autonomously generated tasks, executed model calls, validated configurations, scored outcomes, analyzed results, and drafted the manuscript; per‑step artifacts and hashes are archived. No human manual editing of technical content, numeric results, validator traces, figures, captions, references, or the Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock.
- Deviations and technical failures: A substantive, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered consensus ensemble stage was not executed; this is recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and provider_call audits (stage_counts and condition_counts). Provider/model call failures produced 56 failed episodes (28 task pairs) that were excluded from the primary complete‑pair analysis; this is recorded in analysis/missingness_summary.csv and execution/execution_log.jsonl. The preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') was applied and reported. All deviations, failures, and handling rules are archived and described in the manuscript.
- Human role: The human Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock. After the lock all research formulation, execution, analysis, and manuscript text were generated autonomously; the provenance artifacts above document the autonomy boundary.
- Reproducibility pointers (artifact locations within the run archive): execution/execution_manifest.json (full execution accounting and per‑file SHA‑256s), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces and scoring decisions), execution/responses/*.txt (raw responses), analysis/* (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, paired_difference_figure.svg), execution/model_configuration.json, and provenance/master_prompt.txt (initial master prompt reference SHA‑256 above).
limitations: Single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and long‑horizon workflows.

The preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed in this run (execution manifest stage_counts show only a single shared_initial_generation per task). The executed guarded condition therefore functioned as the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared generation; ensemble effects cannot be inferred from these results.

Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported but failed calls reduce effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects.
